blocks.p: Every Italian noun is masculine or feminine. *Un* and *una* both mean "a"; the noun decides which one you use.
Before a vowel, *una* becomes *un'* with an apostrophe (*un'amica*). *Un* never takes an apostrophe (*un amico*).

examples.en: Good morning. I'd like a cappuccino, please.

text.text: Buongiorno. Vorrei un cappuccino, per favore.

examples.en: No, thanks. Today I'd like a fresh orange juice.

text.text: No, grazie. Oggi vorrei una spremuta.

examples.en: Here comes Sara. Sara is a friend of Marco's.

text.text: Ecco Sara. Sara è un'amica di Marco.

blocks.tip: Most nouns ending in *-o* are masculine and most ending in *-a* are feminine. A noun like *caffè* doesn't tell you, so learn every noun with its article.

intro.textEn: Did you spot it? Marco orders *un cappuccino*, but Sara asks for *una spremuta*.
